summary: Hamilton County steel Aermotor tower of 1924 on a station first set up in 1918; staffed into 1981, radio repeater since 1983, cab closed but stairs reach the top landing.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 9-ft steel-and-glass hip-roof cab; observer's cabin and shed added in 1950

staffing.status: not staffed; solar radio repeater on the tower

access.note: Cab closed to the public; approach roads owned by Lyme Timber, with public access under a conservation easement

visit.trail_note: Hike from the main trailhead at the end of the old service road from Sled Harbor; tower stairs reach a top landing with views; the 2016 NHLR visit flagged repairs to footings and safety netting; roads close in winter

events.note: First wooden station and log cabin, set up by the landowner (Champlain Reality Company, per NHLR); the roster has no entry before 1920
First payroll observer in the roster, May to October 1920
Steel Aermotor LS-40 tower erected; NHLR says operation passed to the state that year
Last observer entry in the payroll roster
Officially decommissioned; forest rangers installed a solar two-way radio repeater on the tower the same year, which the NHLR says is still there
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 31, 2005
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, September 2010
NHLR visit report (November 12, 2016) lists paint, stair and landing work, safety netting and footings needing repair; observer's cabin vandalized and open to the weather

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives the tower as 60 ft (LS-40 with a 9 ft cab). Wikipedia gives 69 ft. No height_m is recorded because the sources disagree.

NHLR (quoting Bill Starr) says the first station was set up in 1918 as a wooden tower with a log cabin, and the state took over in 1924. The payroll roster, which says it is incomplete, begins with a Pillsbury observer in May 1920. The story presents both.

notes_for_editor: Height and early-history dates disagree across sources and are reported as disagreements, not resolved. The roster's own preface calls it an incomplete accounting. Current condition rests on a 2016 NHLR visit report and an undated hiking-guide page; no official DEC source was fetched. A WebSearch summary claimed the tower was closed in 1985 and that it is open except the cab; that claim is not used because no fetched page supports it. A WebSearch summary named a different 1924 observer than the fetched roster does; the story names no observers except Bill Starr, the roster compiler and NHLR registrar, who recalls working there. Roster quotes were checked against the cached PDF text.
